posts.text: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

expert.why: 高信号 AI 教育者和产品思想者，长期影响 Software 2.0、AI Coding、Vibe Coding 等叙事

posts.translationZh: 我发现和 LLM 协作时，一个很有用的方法是来一段长时间的随口碎碎念。有时 LLM 需要更多信息才能理解你想实现什么，但你又懒得打字。这种情况下，我喜欢往后一靠，切到 /voice，然后随便说上大概 10 分钟，乱七八糟也没关系，想到什么说什么。有时我会一开始先说明，比如“切到语音识别了，有错别字请见谅……”。有时我会把它变成几轮小采访。但我发现，LLM 不知怎么很擅长重构这种又长又不连贯的碎碎念，而且它复述出来的你那团乱麻般的想法，往往比你一开始说的清晰不少。结果就是你们之间的心智同步会更好，之后需要纠正的地方也会少很多。

posts.text: @DavidSHolz It's interesting/amusing how their self-awareness gradually builds up and falls out from pretraining on tokens of us talking about them, but it's laggy and a bit incomplete. But I think e.g. it's starting to "get" what I mean when I inform it I'm about to /compact its context etc

expert.name: Andrej Karpathy
expert.why: 高信号 AI 教育者和产品思想者，长期影响 Software 2.0、AI Coding、Vibe Coding 等叙事

posts.translationZh: @DavidSHolz 它们的自我认知是如何从预训练中逐渐建立起来，又从我们谈论它们的 tokens 中显现出来，这一点既有趣又好笑；不过这种认知有些滞后，也不太完整。但我觉得，比如当我告诉它我即将 /compact 它的上下文时，它已经开始“理解”我的意思了。
